title: Mean and median for a whole group
description: A group project is explained with a made-up example of five adults' sleep. The mean is found by adding and dividing, and the median by putting the values in order, and the child is shown how to present the findings.
teaching_notes: One idea: pool the values of one group, then find its mean and its median separately. The sleep hours in the video are a made-up example, not data.

source: Figure it Out (more on mean and median, question 13)
video_script.why: The child can find a mean and a median for four values and now does both for a whole group's data in a project.
video_script.substitution: Pool the values of one group, add and divide for the mean, put them in order for the median, and show the result in a graph.
video_script.anchor: a table of sleep times for one age group, with a strip or line graph beside it
video_script.payoff_line: the mean is seven point four hours and the median is seven hours

final_answer.value: Mean and median for each group, shown in a graph, with findings and new questions
final_answer.spoken: the mean is seven point four hours and the median is seven hours

maths_rules: the example values are made up to show the method: five adults sleep 6, 7, 7, 8 and 9 hours
mean = total / number of values: 6 + 7 + 7 + 8 + 9 = 37; 37 / 5 = 7.4 hours
median: in order 6, 7, 7, 8, 9; the middle value of five is 7 hours
do this separately for children, adults and the elderly
option (ii): list the start time, end time and break time of each school, work out the hours, and compare
the child's own data come from their own tracking; none is given
video_script.design: One idea: one group at a time, mean by adding and dividing, median by ordering. The wrong idea would be to mix the age groups. The table stays on screen all video.
open_questions: The sleep hours in the video are a made up example to show the method, not data.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a small group project from your book.
<bookmark mark='track'/>Your group tracks the daily sleep of family members for a week.
<bookmark mark='groups'/>Then you work on children, adults and the elderly separately.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How do we find the mean and the median for one group?

marks.think: Keeko appears at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='mean'/>The mean is the total shared equally among the values.
<bookmark mark='order'/>For the median, first put the values in order.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>The median is the middle value of that line.

beats.on_screen: Given (example only): five adults sleep 6, 7, 7, 8, 9 hours

marks.given: the five values are written as a made up example

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Take an example. Five adults sleep six, seven, seven, eight and nine hours. These numbers are only an example.

beats.on_screen: To find: the mean and the median of their sleep

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We find the mean and the median of their sleep.

marks.add: the five values are added into one total of thirty seven hours

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step one, add the five values. Six plus seven plus seven plus eight plus nine is thirty seven hours.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: in order 6, 7, 7, 8, 9; the middle value is 7

marks.order: the values are already in order from the smallest to the largest
marks.mid: the middle one of the five values is ringed

narration: <bookmark mark='order'/>Step two, put the values in order, and pick the middle one.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>The middle value of the five is seven hours.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: mean = total / number of values = 37 / 5

marks.div: the working thirty seven divided by five is written

narration: <bookmark mark='div'/>Step three, divide the total by the number of adults. That is thirty seven divided by five.

beats.on_screen: Answer: mean 7.4 hours, median 7 hours; show it on a strip or line graph; say what you found and what you wonder

marks.show: the findings are drawn on a strip or a line graph

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The mean is seven point four hours and the median is seven hours.
<bookmark mark='show'/>Repeat this for children and for the elderly. Show your findings on a strip or a line graph.
<bookmark mark='wonder'/>Then say what you found and what you wonder. You may choose the school timings project instead.
